### ⚠️ REQ-56811be1

**Requirement:** M19 drift-detection precision eval on loom-self: N=17 (target was 30-50), precision 100% (17 TP, 0 FP, 0 Ambig). HEADLINE IS NOT THE PRECISION NUMBER — it's the sample-composition finding: 12 of 17 cases are file-inception events; zero are cosmetic-only commits. Sample structurally cannot produce FPs because the 10 linked impls have short commit histories without enough cosmetic/refactor noise to populate negative bins. Pre-registered prediction of 50-70% precision was wrong because it assumed baseline cosmetic-commit volume that doesn't exist on this codebase's linked-file subset. The eval as designed measures detector-correctness-on-existing-history, NOT real-world FP rate in working dev loops. Three follow-up pivots: M19v2 (enrich link count first), M19v3 (synthetic-edit eval to populate FP bin), or stop and accept the finding about self-eval limitations.

### ⚠️ REQ-6834d5b6

**Requirement:** M19v2 enriched drift-eval (linked impls 10→30 via auto-link, N=76, 58 drift-fires + 18 TN): 58/58 classified TP via heuristic, precision 100%. THREE production bugs surfaced + fixed in the process: (1) services._read_file_content used system default encoding (cp1252 on Windows) failing on UTF-8 source with em-dashes; (2) _ollama_embed silently fell back to hash on HTTP 400 from nomic-embed-text's ~7K-char context limit, producing similarity NOISE reported to users as real matches; (3) spurious auto-links from hash-fallback noise (rolled back). The 100% precision number is honest but limited — measures 'file content actually changed' (trivially correct by SHA256) not 'change violates linked req intent' (req-relevance precision unmeasured). Predicted-band 50-70% was wrong both v1 and v2; intuition about cosmetic-commit ratio in Python codebases doesn't match reality. Methodology pattern 9/9: predicted-band lock forced honest surfacing of the wrong-prediction even when result direction is favorable.

ClangdIndexer Phase 1 is not the C++ lever; further investment requires either embedding LLM-summarized contract prose into context_for, or piloting Kythe (Phase 2) for project-wide queries that clangd cannot answer.

### ⚠️ REQ-c38ea918

**Requirement:** M10.2 replication at N=10 on the locked S1 C++ benchmark CONFIRMS H1 (rat cell in [30%, 70%]): 4/10 = 40% (Wilson 95% CI 17-69%). All three H2 sanity checks pass (off 20% <= 30%, on-rule 0% <= 50%, placebo 60% >= 30%). The M10.2 effect is REAL and reproducible -- not the N=5 Type I error I expected. The locked predictors prior (60% refute / 30% confirm / 10% inconclusive) was overturned by the data: H1 confirmed at the central band. The CONSEQUENCE for the C++ S1 narrative: the M10.2 stubs carrier is empirically load-bearing, but it consists of unverifiable hand-crafted context (fictional call sites at src/backoff_loop.hpp + src/sync_worker.cpp -- files that do NOT exist in the scenario; an invented "production incident 2024-09-12" anchor). Real LSP refs (M28) and LLM-summarized prose constrained to real files (M28v2) both produce 0%. The mechanism appears to be: qwen2.5-coder:32b treats plausibly-shaped unverifiable context as authoritative weight on the contrarian rule. This is NOT a Loom-deployable feature. It IS a methodologically important finding about LLM weighting of plausibility vs verifiability. The honest workplace claim becomes: "On C++ S1, we identified a reproducible 40pp lift, but the mechanism requires hand-crafted unverifiable context the executor accepts as authoritative -- not a scalable deployment pattern, but a finding about LLM behavior in the presence of plausible fabrication."
